newsitem.title: UK: Johnson Matthey profits defy gloomy metals.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey profits defy gloomy metals.

text.p: Johnson Matthey, the British precious metals and industrial materials company, said on Thursday that pre-tax profits rose by nine percent to 51.2 million pounds ($85.96 million) in a first half battle against the odds.

"The recovery of catalytic systems has been exemplary and profit growth shown in the first half will continue," Chairman David Davies said in comments on the results which stressed the difficult trading conditions .
"However, in the short term it is unlikely that the markets in which our precious metals and ceramics businesses operate will improve."

The results, in line with analysts' expectations, were a tale of contrasting fortunes, with profits powered by a 15 percent increase in earnings in the electronic materials division and a 22 percent recovery in catalytic systems.
However, precious metals and ceramics chugged along in the slow lane, reaching the mid-year stage with flat profits.

This tempered a generally bullish market reaction which saw the share price rise 12p to 546p by 1120 GMT. The price had dropped this year from a high of 669p against a background of soft demand for ceramic products and weak platinum prices.
"This is a bounce on relief. There was a lot of talk about a horror scenario and that has weighed on the shares. But these are by no means a stunning set of figures," one dealer said.

Overall sales were up only two percent from the first half of last year, but operating profits increased eight percent to 55.3 million stg. Earnings per share were up three percent at 16.9p. The interim dividend rose seven percent to 4.7p.

Davies said the short-term outlook for precious metals was not encouraging. "But demand from the jewellery and industrial sectors is expected to continue to grow and the longer term fundamentals for platinum are positive."
He said the electronics division did well despite a downturn in the semiconductor industry.
Gordon Thorburn, executive director for administration, told Reuters that the electronics results reflected strong input by subsidiary Advance Circuits Inc, acquired last year.

"We have also made good progress with our plastic laminate packages project. That will make some money in the second half and is the principal reason for us being quite enthusiastic about our prospects for next year in that division," he said.
Thorburn said the microelectronics market was generally difficult. "Sales are actually down in that market in the current year, so we're pleased with our progress there."
The catalytic systems division was boosted by healthy world car markets.
"But in ceramics the markets have been getting quite difficult with the depression in the German construction industry, which affects the tile industry," Thorburn said.
Depressed European tile markets held back growth at the Cookson Matthey Ceramics division.
